body:
The 3 essential characteristics of armoured vehicles

An armoured military vehicle combines some degree of protection, mobility and firepower. The balance differs according to the vehicle's role.

  • Protection: Armour and other safety systems help protect personnel and equipment from specified threats.
  • Mobility: The vehicle must travel over relevant terrain while carrying its crew, equipment and supplies.
  • Firepower: Where applicable, onboard weapons provide a combat capability.

These characteristics involve trade-offs. Increasing protection may increase weight. Greater weight can affect bridge use, transport, fuel requirements and movement over soft ground. A lighter vehicle may be easier to transport but generally offers a different level of protection from a heavy tank.

Main battle tank, infantry fighting vehicle and personnel carrier

Vehicle categoryPrincipal purposeTypical characteristic
Main battle tank (MBT)Armoured combatSubstantial protection and a powerful main gun
Infantry fighting vehicle (IFV)Transport infantry and support them in combatArmoured personnel compartment and onboard weapons
Armoured personnel carrier (APC)Move personnel under armour protectionTransport is its main function
Light tankTank-like capability with lower vehicle weightDesigned for mobility or transport constraints different from those of an MBT

The most important distinction is that an MBT is primarily a combat vehicle, while an IFV combines infantry transport with direct combat support. An APC principally carries personnel under protection. The exact equipment carried varies by design, and classifications can overlap.

Tracked and wheeled mobility

Tracked vehicles

A tracked vehicle spreads its weight over a relatively large contact area through continuous tracks. This can improve movement over certain soft or uneven surfaces. Tracks also involve maintenance requirements and do not guarantee good performance on every terrain.

Wheeled vehicles

Wheeled military vehicles can be efficient on roads and are often suitable for long-distance movement. Their off-road ability depends on tyre design, vehicle weight, suspension, drive arrangement and ground conditions.

A vehicle's ability to cross a route also depends on whether roads, slopes, bridges and other physical features can support it. Ground pressure helps explain why spreading weight over a larger area can reduce pressure on soft ground. The relationship follows the elementary principle that pressure depends on force and the area over which it acts.

Indian armoured vehicle examples

Arjun is an indigenously developed Indian main battle tank associated with DRDO's Combat Vehicles Research and Development Establishment (CVRDE). The T-90 is another main battle tank used by the Indian Army.

The BMP-2 is an infantry combat vehicle used by the Indian Army. It illustrates the difference between carrying infantry in an armoured vehicle and operating a dedicated main battle tank. In March 2024, the Ministry of Defence signed a contract for upgrades to BMP-2 vehicles, including improvements relating to sights and fire-control equipment.

Zorawar is an Indian light-tank development programme involving DRDO's CVRDE and Larsen & Toubro. DRDO announced successful preliminary automotive and developmental firing trials on 13 September 2024. Those trials were a development milestone; the announcement should not be read as proof of operational induction on the same date.

Mobility beyond the vehicle itself

Military mobility also depends on fuel, spare parts, repair facilities, transport vehicles, roads and bridges. An armoured vehicle that can cross rough ground may still face limitations caused by bridge capacity or the availability of maintenance. Consequently, logistics—the provision and movement of necessary supplies and support—is a fundamental part of land-system effectiveness.

Prelims focus

  • MBT means main battle tank; IFV means infantry fighting vehicle; APC means armoured personnel carrier.
  • An IFV carries infantry and supports them in combat, while an APC is primarily a protected transport vehicle.
  • Arjun is an indigenous Indian main battle tank associated with DRDO's CVRDE.
  • BMP-2 is an infantry combat vehicle used by the Indian Army.
  • Zorawar's developmental trials were reported on 13 September 2024.
  • Trap: Tracks can improve mobility on some soft surfaces, but they do not make a vehicle suitable for every route or bridge.

[Sources: NCERT, Science, Class 8, Ch. 11, 'Force and Pressure', and Ch. 12, 'Friction'; Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Defence, 'MoD inks contract with AVNL for 693 Armament Upgrades of Infantry Combat Vehicle BMP2 to BMP2M', 13 March 2024; 'DRDO successfully conducts first phase of Developmental Field Firing Trials of Indian Light Tank Zorawar', 13 September 2024; consulted 14 November 2026.]

title: Land Combat Vehicles: Armour, Infantry Carriers and Battlefield Mobility

body:
What artillery means

Artillery refers broadly to military weapons designed to deliver fire beyond the ordinary capabilities of individual infantry small arms. Artillery includes different weapon categories with distinct physical arrangements and roles.

A common distinction is between direct fire and indirect fire. In direct fire, the weapon is aimed towards a target that can be observed through the applicable sighting system. In indirect fire, a weapon fires towards a target that is not necessarily visible from the weapon's position; information from observation and communication is used to determine whether the required target area has been reached.

These are general descriptions of methods of employment. They do not mean that every weapon must be classified exclusively as either direct-fire or indirect-fire equipment in all circumstances.

Major artillery categories

CategoryBasic characteristicPrincipal distinction
Field gunConventional gun artilleryHistorically associated with relatively flatter trajectories
HowitzerArtillery gun capable of high-angle fireCommonly used for indirect artillery support
MortarGenerally a shorter-barrelled, high-angle weaponUseful where a steep projectile path is required
Rocket artilleryLaunches rocket-propelled projectilesProjectile propulsion differs from that of a conventional gun-fired shell

Modern artillery categories overlap more than their historical definitions suggest. Some modern guns and howitzers can use a wide range of firing angles. The essential prelims distinction is between a conventional tube-artillery projectile and a rocket that generates thrust through its own propulsion system.

Towed and self-propelled artillery

Towed artillery is moved between locations by a separate towing vehicle, although some systems may have limited auxiliary movement capability. A self-propelled artillery system carries its artillery weapon on a powered vehicle.

Self-propelled artillery can be mounted on tracks or wheels. It should not be confused with an ordinary main battle tank merely because both can have tracks and large guns. A tank is designed primarily for armoured combat; a self-propelled howitzer is an artillery platform.

Indian examples

Advanced Towed Artillery Gun System

ATAGS stands for Advanced Towed Artillery Gun System. It is an indigenous artillery programme associated with DRDO's Armament Research and Development Establishment and Indian industry.

On 26 March 2025, the Ministry of Defence signed procurement contracts for 155 mm/52 calibre ATAGS and associated gun-towing vehicles. The designation identifies a 155 mm artillery system with a barrel length of 52 times its nominal bore diameter. The 2025 event was a contract milestone, not a statement that every contracted system had already been delivered.

K9 Vajra-T

K9 Vajra-T is a 155 mm/52 calibre tracked self-propelled artillery system. It combines a howitzer with a powered tracked vehicle. A Ministry of Defence contract announced on 20 December 2024 concerned additional K9 Vajra-T systems.

M777

The M777 is a 155 mm lightweight towed howitzer. Its classification differs from the tracked self-propelled K9 Vajra-T. Both belong to tube artillery, but their mobility arrangements are different.

Pinaka

Pinaka is India's indigenous multiple-barrel rocket-launcher system. It belongs to rocket artillery rather than conventional towed or self-propelled tube howitzers. DRDO announced successful tests of a guided Pinaka weapon-system variant on 14 November 2024. Testing a guided variant should not be confused with the original system's entire history or with immediate induction of that tested variant.

Prelims focus

  • ATAGS means Advanced Towed Artillery Gun System.
  • ATAGS is a 155 mm/52 calibre system; procurement contracts were signed on 26 March 2025.
  • K9 Vajra-T is a tracked self-propelled 155 mm/52 calibre artillery system.
  • M777 is a lightweight towed 155 mm howitzer.
  • Pinaka is a multiple-barrel rocket-launcher system.
  • Trap: Pinaka is rocket artillery; ATAGS, M777 and K9 Vajra-T are tube-artillery systems.

[Sources: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Defence, 'Aatmanirbhar Bharat: MoD inks contracts for 155mm/52 Calibre Advanced Towed Artillery Gun Systems & High Mobility Vehicle 6x6 Gun Towing Vehicles', 26 March 2025; 'MoD inks contract with L&T for K9 VAJRA-T Self-Propelled Tracked Artillery Guns', 20 December 2024; 'DRDO successfully completes Flight Tests of Guided Pinaka Weapon System', 14 November 2024; consulted 14 November 2026.]

body:
Meaning of small arms

Small arms generally refers to firearms designed for use by individual personnel. They differ from larger crew-served artillery and vehicle-mounted systems in their size, intended role and operating arrangement.

For prelims preparation, the most useful distinctions concern the broad category of weapon, its intended use and the terminology used to describe its characteristics. A weapon's name, calibre and classification do not by themselves tell us every detail of its performance.

Common categories

CategoryBasic characteristicGeneral role
PistolCompact handgunIndividual sidearm
RifleShoulder-fired firearm with a rifled barrelGeneral infantry individual weapon
CarbineGenerally a shorter, more compact shoulder-fired firearmUsed where compactness is important
Machine gunFirearm designed to provide automatic fireInfantry or vehicle fire-support role
Light machine gun (LMG)Relatively portable machine-gun categoryInfantry team fire support

These are broad conventional categories. Some modern firearms may share features from more than one category, and actual classifications can depend on military terminology and design.

What rifling means

A rifled barrel has spiral grooves or an equivalent rifling arrangement that makes a suitable projectile rotate as it travels through the barrel. The resulting spin can help stabilise the projectile in flight.

A smoothbore barrel lacks conventional rifling. The words rifled and smoothbore describe the barrel interior; they are not synonyms for automatic and non-automatic operation.

Calibre and the meaning of weapon designations

Calibre usually refers to a characteristic internal barrel diameter or projectile diameter, depending on the measurement convention. It may be expressed in millimetres. However, the same nominal calibre does not automatically establish that ammunition, components or weapon systems are interchangeable.

In conventional artillery naming, 155 mm/52 calibre uses 155 mm to indicate the nominal bore diameter and 52 calibre to indicate a barrel length of 52 times that diameter. This use of the word calibre differs from simply referring to a rifle's nominal ammunition diameter.

Individual weapons and larger battlefield systems

A soldier's individual firearm is only one part of land-system capability. Safe communication, protected mobility, observation, identification, medical support and logistics remain necessary. A larger calibre does not automatically make a weapon appropriate for every task, and a faster-firing weapon is not necessarily the most useful equipment for every situation.

Keep 3 distinctions separate: A weapon's category describes its general role; rifling describes a feature of its barrel; calibre describes a dimensional characteristic under the relevant naming convention.

Prelims focus

  • A rifle is a shoulder-fired firearm associated with a rifled barrel.
  • A carbine is generally shorter and more compact than a conventional rifle.
  • LMG means light machine gun.
  • Rifling imparts spin that can help stabilise a projectile.
  • Trap: Rifling, calibre and automatic operation describe different firearm characteristics.

[Sources: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Defence, 'National Defence Industries Association exhibition and Indian Army equipment display', March 2024, section listing Indian Army rifles and small arms; Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Defence, 'MoD inks contracts for 155mm/52 Calibre Advanced Towed Artillery Gun Systems', 26 March 2025; consulted 14 November 2026.]
title: Infantry Small Arms: Basic Types and Terminology
